newsitem.title: USA: U.S. high court to hear affirmative action appeal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. high court to hear affirmative action appeal.

text.p: The Supreme Court on Friday agreed to review whether racial diversity can be outlawed as a basis for workplace decisions in an affirmative action case that led the Clinton administration to shift its position.

The high court said it would review the closely watched ruling that a New Jersey school district may not take racial diversity into account when laying off a white teacher over an equally qualified black teacher.

The Clinton Justice Department earlier this month took the awkward position of urging the high court to leave in place the ruling, even though the administration did not agree with it. Department lawyers urged the high court not to review the case.
At issue was an appeal by the Board of Education in Piscataway arguing that employers may consider race as a factor in layoff decisions for purposes other than to remedy past discrimination.

The school board argued that fostering diversity on a high school faculty was a lawful purpose and said consideration of race in layoff decisions does not invariably violate the rights of white employees.

The high court action was a setback for Justice Department lawyers, who privately expressed concern the court might use the case to further restrict, if not end altogether, certain affirmative action programs for blacks and other minorities.
